rationale: Three independent times now, a model property validated on the full skill-position player population has failed to transfer -- or reversed -- on the subpopulation Kalshi actually lists. (1) Role features improve calibrated ladder probabilities in 6/6 statistics on the full ladder and are worth ~0 on Kalshi-listed players (-0.00010 +- 0.00068) and slightly negative on Kalshi's own rungs (+0.00117 +- 0.00104). (2) The model's tail defect is a long-shot OVERstatement on the full ladder (-0.0096 at p 0.02-0.05, z=-11.7) and a long-shot UNDERstatement on Kalshi rungs (+0.0369). (3) The LadderCalibrator built to correct the first therefore does the reverse of its stated purpose on the traded population. The proposed mechanism is shrinkage: a position prior that is right on average pulls bench players up and established starters down, and Kalshi lists starters.
features: any feature or calibration validated on a full-population ladder
target: the sign and magnitude of the validated effect when re-measured on Kalshi-listed contracts only
expected_direction: Effects validated on the full population will attenuate toward zero or reverse on Kalshi-listed contracts, with the reversal concentrated where position-prior shrinkage is largest. A feature that survives full-population validation should NOT be assumed to survive on the traded population without direct re-measurement.
test_plan: Standing rule rather than a single test: every future feature or calibration claim is measured twice, once on the full population and once restricted to Kalshi-listed contracts, and the traded-population figure is the one that counts. Pre-specified failure criterion for the mechanism: if a future effect transfers cleanly with no attenuation, the shrinkage explanation is wrong and this is downgraded.
result: Three for three so far: role features (transfer to ~0), tail defect (sign reversal), calibrator direction (reversal). No counterexample yet. DECISION EXECUTED: on 24,731 settled 2025 Kalshi rungs across 254 games the role arm is +0.00029 +- 0.00072 Brier vs base (z=+0.41) and improves 0 of 6 statistics at |z|>2. Role features are now OFF by default in the shadow pricer (use_role_features, default False); the frozen Week-1 arm shadow-0.3.0 passes the flag explicitly to stay reproducible.
notes: Registered as a methodological hypothesis because it has already cost this project two headline results. It also implies that the entire session-2 opportunity-engine programme was validated on the wrong population, and that any future 'the model improved' claim is meaningless unless measured on listed contracts.
status_note: STATUS IS CORRECT AS REGISTERED_PROSPECTIVE AND SHOULD NOT BE FLIPPED TO RETIRED. H-022 is a standing methodological rule -- 'measure every claim on the traded population, not the full one' -- not a feature. What was RETIRED in session 4 is the ROLE FEATURES, which is a consequence of applying this rule, and is recorded in `decision_executed` below. The rule itself stays live because every future feature claim is tested against it, and it carries an explicit falsifier: an effect that transfers cleanly with no attenuation would disconfirm the shrinkage explanation.
